title: Liquid Cell Transmission Electron Microscopy and Molecular Dynamics Assisted Microanalysis for Biomolecular Assemblies
content: Biomolecular assemblies, which define the spatial and temporal arrangement of biomolecules into functional structures, are present in most if not all processes in life. It not only enables us to uncover the secrets of life formation but also reveals pivot points for humans to understand unnormal molecules assembly, develop drugs, and tackle diseases [1]. Among the processes in biomolecular assemblies, liquid liquid-phase separation (LLPS) and self-assembly are highly conservative in evolution, marking their irreplaceable roles in life.[2, 3] LLPS is a process in which a homogeneous solution separates into one condensed phase and one depleted phase. It is essential for the formation of membraneless organelles but also participates in viral infection and Alzheimer's disease pathogenesis [2]. Self-assembly defines the process in which disordered molecules spontaneously organize into ordered structures through local interactions. It participates in the formation of cell skeletons in cells and protein misfolding diseases [3-5].
